question: Should OpenClaw adopt `@openclaw/localization-core` and `OPENCLAW_LOCALE` as the shared cross-product localization contract, and should this cumulative adoption slice proceed only after the foundation lands?
rationale: The patch adds a broad runtime/package boundary, user-visible environment behavior, and a repository-wide check; code review cannot determine whether that is the intended permanent product architecture.

options.title: Approve dependency-first series
options.body: Approve the shared runtime direction, land the foundation independently, then require this PR to rebase as a focused adoption slice with real CLI proof.

options.title: Narrow the contract
options.body: Keep localization surface-owned and remove or defer the shared package, environment-variable expansion, or global coverage check until a smaller proposal is approved.

options.title: Pause the series
options.body: Pause this PR until the RFC and maintainers settle ownership, supported locale scope, and rollout expectations.

recommendation.title: Approve dependency-first series
recommendation.body: Approve the shared runtime direction, land the foundation independently, then require this PR to rebase as a focused adoption slice with real CLI proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the linked localization series and can clarify its intended boundary, while a repository maintainer must make the final product decision.
